a: A hidden-role mafia party game for a room of friends, the game Greeks know as Palermo, a cousin of Mafia and Werewolf. Your phone holds your secret card, the TV shows the town, and a noir narrator runs every night, so nobody has to sit out to lead the game.

q: How many players do we need?
a: From 6 to 14. By default the town hides two killers up to 11 players, and three from 12. The host picks the roles and the timers before the deal, or starts from a preset: Classic, Quick or Full house.

q: What do we need to play?
a: A phone each, iPhone or Android, and one screen the whole room can see: a Samsung or LG smart TV from 2022 on, an Android TV, or a laptop on the TV. Any phone in the room taps Show on TV: open vgraphics.gr/tv on the screen and type the twelve-digit TV code it gives, or open its link. The screen then shows the room's code and a QR code, which friends scan to join. Nothing to install: the whole game plays in the browser.

q: Which TVs can show the town?
a: Samsung and LG smart TVs from 2022 on, an Android TV, or a laptop on the TV over HDMI: Palermo Noir runs in their browser. Other TVs may still play on a lighter TV page, which opens by itself when a TV's browser can't keep up. Samsung and LG sets from before 2022 can't run it, and the screen says so and names the TVs that can.
Yes, with every role in. Ads only show outside play, between games and never during one.

No. Join as a guest, or with your free VHub name, which keeps your games, XP and achievements across every VGraphics game. Signed in with a VHub photo, it shows for your seat on the TV and on every phone, the guided demo too, unless you turn on Use my character's picture instead in the phone's menu; without a photo, your character's portrait shows. The VHub button at the top right of the start screen signs you in or opens your profile. The TV signs in as a screen, never as a person.

q: How do I add a friend?
a: Tap another player in a room's lobby, or their seat on the phone's Table tab during the game and after it, then Add friend on their card. They get your request on VHub and in their notifications, and once they accept you are friends in every VGraphics game. You can also add friends by name or friend code on VHub. On a card, sign in first; as a guest you can still add friends by friend code on VHub.
It's for ages 13 and up. Each phone gives its year of birth once and only an age group is kept, never the year.
English or Greek. The narrator, the cards and every screen follow the host's language.

q: Can we share how the night went?
a: Yes. When a game ends, Share the night on every phone at the table draws the evening as a picture to post or send: the town paper, a film poster, your secret card, the newsreel or the whole table, each with a QR code back to Palermo. The TV shows a QR code too, so friends who only watched can share it as well. The phone draws the picture itself; nothing is uploaded. The guided demo ends with it as well, drawing your own secret card without naming who the killers were.

Now: rooms are open. Tap Play online, and the game runs in a phone's or a PC's browser, iPhones included. The host creates a room, friends join with its code or the QR code on the TV, and the TV opens vgraphics.gr/tv. Nothing to install; an Android app comes later. To learn it alone first, the guided demo seats you at a table of bots, and its pause menu lets you resume, open Settings or exit whenever you like. Every release shows under What's new on this page.

A room closes 30 minutes after its last phone goes offline, or 8 hours after it opened, and is deleted 24 hours after it closes. A short summary of each game, with no names, identifiers or votes, is kept for 12 months. Analytics runs only with your consent. The privacy policy has the details.

q: What are the newsreels on the TV?
a: The first time a big moment happens in a game, the TV plays it as the town's 1947 newsreel: a killer arrested or an innocent voted out, a card that stays face down, a body at dawn or a quiet night, a tie, the Hunter's last shot, the Lovers' broken heart, the Kamikaze's blast, the Mayor standing up, and at the end the town's, the killers', the Madman's or the Lovers' win. There are fifteen, each a short film set at its own place on the town map, in the gold frame of the role cards, with the characters' lines in the room's language, English or Greek. Each plays once a game.

q: Where can I read the rules?
a: In the wiki: every role, every card in the Lawyer's briefcase, and how a round plays, from the deal to the verdict.
